name: How long does a full home renovation planning phase take in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: How long does it usually take to plan a full home renovation before construction starts in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: How long does it usually take to plan a full home renovation before construction starts in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full home renovation planning phase in Los Angeles usually takes longer than homeowners expect because it includes concept design, field measurements, engineering, permit strategy, and city review. For a straightforward interior remodel, planning may take about 4 to 6 weeks. For a kitchen, whole-floor remodel, or project involving structural changes, the timeline commonly stretches to 3 to 6 months. If the plan includes wall removal, grading, hillside conditions, or multiple agency reviews, planning can take even longer. The biggest time drivers are design revisions, engineering coordination, and whether the project needs plan check. Homeowners should expect at least one round of corrections after submittal for anything beyond basic cosmetic work. The safest approach is to build schedule buffer before selecting a start date or ordering long-lead materials. A contractor or design-build team can often shorten the process by coordinating plans, permit documents, and submittal requirements early.
acceptedAnswer.description: A full home renovation planning phase in Los Angeles often takes several weeks to several months, depending on design complexity, engineering, and permit needs. Simple interior remodels may move in 4 to 6 weeks, while larger projects with structural changes, additions, or ADU-like elements can take 3 to 6 months or longer before work begins.
